title: Estimate capacity with everyday referents (how many mugs make a litre?)

lesson.title: How Many Mugs Make a Litre?

steps.say: You already know that one thousand millilitres makes one litre. Today we will use that fact in real life, so you can look at a mug or a bottle and guess how much it holds without any measuring cup at all.

The trick is to keep one everyday thing in your head as a helper. We call it a referent. A regular mug of hot chocolate holds about two hundred and fifty millilitres. So four mugs fill up one whole litre, because two hundred and fifty times four is one thousand.

visual.caption: Counting up by 250 mL: four mugs make 1000 mL, which is one litre

steps.say: Here are some more helpers you can carry around in your memory. A teaspoon is about five millilitres, a can of pop is about three hundred and fifty five millilitres, a milk carton at school is about two hundred and fifty millilitres, and a big carton of milk from the grocery store is four litres.

Let's try one. Grandma is making soup and her pot holds about three litres. She fills it using her mug. About how many mugs will she need? Three litres is three thousand millilitres, and each mug is two hundred and fifty millilitres. Four mugs make one litre, so for three litres it is four times three, which is twelve mugs.

Here is a mistake that trips lots of kids up. Some people see the number three and the number two hundred fifty and think, three mugs make three litres, one each. But that forgets the size of the mug. A mug is much smaller than a litre, so you always need more mugs than litres, never fewer. Whenever your answer says fewer small things than big things, stop and check.

visual.caption: Smaller container means you need more of them

steps.say: So pick a helper you know well, ask yourself how many of them fit inside, and you can estimate any container you meet.

lesson.answer: A mug holds about 250 mL, so 4 mugs make 1 litre — smaller container, more of them!

practice.question: At a soccer game in Surrey, the team cooler holds five litres of water. Each player's small water bottle holds about five hundred millilitres. About how many bottles can be filled from the full cooler? Try drawing five long bars for the five litres, and see how many bottles fit in each one.
practice.answer: Ten bottles. Five litres is five thousand millilitres, and each litre fills two bottles of five hundred millilitres, so five times two is ten.
